text: writing analysis code, need define populations phenotypes. happens inputs/ folder. two types inputs cohorts concept sets. Picard helps organize inputs file called manifest. sqlite file disk tracks meta data inputs per type. full examples follow loding_inputs manifest_overview vignettes. start initializing manifest, creates sqlite file track assets. example show load cohorts atlas. create blank load file need fill pull cohorts atlas. blank csv file columns : atlasId: ATLAS cohort definition IDs (required) label: Display name cohort (required) category: Broad category like “Disease Populations”, “Treatment Groups” (required) subCategory: Optional sub-grouping within category filled connect WebApi pull cohorts repo. code gives example workflow. process inputing concept sets similar. also ways add inputs manifest : Individual $addAtlasCohort() - Downloads cohort ATLAS ID, writes JSON disk, registers manifest. Bulk Import $importAtlasCohorts() - Imports multiple ATLAS cohorts load dataframe (atlasId/label/category + optional tags). Circe cohorts file $addCirceCohort() - Register circe-compatible JSON disk manifest. Capr Cohorts $addCaprCohort() - Registers Capr cohort object exporting JSON adding manifest. Sql Cohorts $addSqlCohort() - Registers hand-written SQL cohort file base cohort manifest. $buildCensorCohort() - Censors target cohort censoring event cohort. $buildCompositeCohort() - Creates cohort requiring membership across multiple parent cohorts. $buildComplementCohort() - Creates cohort population cohort excluding selected cohorts. $buildUnionCohort() - Unions multiple parent cohorts single derived cohort. $buildSubsetCohortTemporal() - Subsets base cohort using temporal rules relative filter cohort. $buildTPriorO() - Builds target events prior outcome logic. $buildOPriorT() - Builds outcome events prior target logic. $buildDemographicCohort() - Subsets base cohort demographic criteria (age/sex/race/ethnicity). Custom Dependent Cohorts: $addDependentCustomCohort() - Registers dependency-aware custom SQL named parent cohort parameters. Individual $addAtlasConceptSet() - Downloads concept set ATLAS ID, writes JSON disk, registers manifest. Bulk Import $importAtlasConceptSets() - Imports multiple ATLAS concept sets load dataframe (atlasId/label/category + optional tags). Capr Concept Sets $addCaprConceptSet() - Converts Capr concept set object JSON registers manifest. Combine Concept Sets $combineConceptSets() - Combine concept sets existing manifest make new concept set

text: parameterized SQL queries used SqlRender, create files analysis/src/sql/ using makeSrcSqlFile(): creates standardized SQL file analysis/src/sql/drug_exposure_summary.sql placeholders SqlRender parameters. Important: SqlRender uses @paramName notation substitution. ’s realistic example builds intermediate work table multi-step logic: Best Practice: Wrap SQL queries utility functions stored analysis/src/ files, call functions tasks. keeps SQL execution logic organized reusable: call function task file: Workflow Summary: 1. SQL file creates intermediate work table computed values 2. R function orchestrates render → translate → execute → collect 3. Task file sources utility function gets back dataframe 4. database configuration comes ExecutionSettings
code: makeSrcSqlFile(   fileName = "drug_exposure_summary",   author = "Jane Doe",   description = "Create a summary table of drug exposure by observation period" ) /*  Document your parameters at the top:   @cdmDatabaseSchema - Schema containing OMOP CDM tables   @workDatabaseSchema - Schema for output tables   @workTableName - Name of the intermediate work table to create   @studyStartDate - Start date for filtering   @studyEndDate - End date for filtering */  -- Create intermediate table of drug exposures by observation period CREATE TABLE @workDatabaseSchema.@workTableName AS  WITH obs_periods AS (   -- Get all observation periods for study participants   SELECT      person_id,     observation_period_start_date,     observation_period_end_date   FROM @cdmDatabaseSchema.observation_period   WHERE observation_period_start_date >= '@studyStartDate'     AND observation_period_start_date <= '@studyEndDate' ),  drug_exp AS (   -- Get drug exposures during these observation periods   SELECT     d.person_id,     op.observation_period_start_date,     op.observation_period_end_date,     d.drug_concept_id,     d.drug_exposure_start_date,     COALESCE(d.drug_exposure_end_date, d.drug_exposure_start_date) AS drug_exposure_end_date,     COALESCE(d.days_supply, 1) AS days_supply   FROM @cdmDatabaseSchema.drug_exposure d   JOIN obs_periods op     ON d.person_id = op.person_id     AND d.drug_exposure_start_date >= op.observation_period_start_date     AND d.drug_exposure_start_date <= op.observation_period_end_date ),  person_summary AS (   -- Aggregate to person-level summaries   SELECT     person_id,     observation_period_start_date,     observation_period_end_date,     COUNT(DISTINCT drug_concept_id) AS num_unique_drugs,     COUNT(DISTINCT drug_exposure_start_date) AS num_drug_exposures,     SUM(days_supply) AS total_days_supply,     AVG(days_supply) AS avg_days_supply,     MIN(drug_exposure_start_date) AS first_drug_date,     MAX(drug_exposure_end_date) AS last_drug_date   FROM drug_exp   GROUP BY person_id, observation_period_start_date, observation_period_end_date )  SELECT * FROM person_summary; # Example utility function in analysis/src/execute_sql_queries.R  get_drug_exposure_summary <- function(executionSettings,                                       workTableName = "drug_exposure_summary",                                       studyStartDate = "2020-01-01",                                       studyEndDate = "2023-12-31") {   # Read the SQL file   sql <- readr::read_file(here::here("analysis/src/sql/drug_exposure_summary.sql"))      # Step 1: Render parameters using SqlRender   rendered_drug_sql <- SqlRender::render(     sql,     cdmDatabaseSchema = executionSettings$cdmDatabaseSchema,     workDatabaseSchema = executionSettings$workDatabaseSchema,     workTableName = workTableName,     studyStartDate = studyStartDate,     studyEndDate = studyEndDate   )      # Step 2: Translate to DBMS dialect   # The ExecutionSettings object knows your DBMS type and tempEmulationSchema   translated_drug_sql <- SqlRender::translate(     rendered_drug_sql,     targetDialect = executionSettings$getDbms(),     tempEmulationSchema = executionSettings$tempEmulationSchema   )      # Get the connection from ExecutionSettings   connection <- executionSettings$getConnection()      # If connection is null, establish one   if (is.null(connection)) {     executionSettings$connect()     connection <- executionSettings$getConnection()   }      # Step 3: Execute the query to create the work table   DatabaseConnector::executeSql(connection, translated_drug_sql)      # Step 4: Query the created table to retrieve results   # Use SqlRender and translate for the SELECT query as well   select_query <- "SELECT * FROM @workDatabaseSchema.@workTableName"      rendered_select <- SqlRender::render(     select_query,     workDatabaseSchema = executionSettings$workDatabaseSchema,     workTableName = workTableName   )      translated_select <- SqlRender::translate(     rendered_select,     targetDialect = executionSettings$getDbms(),     tempEmulationSchema = executionSettings$tempEmulationSchema   )      results <- DatabaseConnector::querySql(connection, translated_select)      # Disconnect from the database   executionSettings$disconnect()      cli::cli_alert_success("Drug exposure summary retrieved successfully")      return(results) } # In your task file (e.g., 02_drug_exposure_analysis.R) source(here::here("analysis/src/execute_sql_queries.R"))  # Execute the SQL query and collect results drug_summary <- get_drug_exposure_summary(   executionSettings = executionSettings,   workTableName = "drug_exp_summary",   studyStartDate = "2020-01-01",   studyEndDate = "2023-12-31" )  # Now work with results in R head(drug_summary)

title: Evidence Generation Plan
text: Evidence Generation Plan (EGP) required document Picard pipeline. structured specification document bridges research questions analysis code. EGP defines analytical experiment layman’s terms drives pipeline—code implements specifications document . serves three critical purposes: Precision: Translates research questions exact analytical specifications (numerators, denominators, observation windows, inclusion/exclusion logic) Transparency: Makes choices explicit justified, enabling others understand validate approach Implementation: Provides sufficient detail programmers can implement vision without ambiguity Key insight: EGPs one-size-fits-templates. adapt fundamentally based study design: Surveillance studies (prevalence, incidence) emphasize observation periods, lookback windows, numerator/denominator specifications (example: Type 2 Diabetes prevalence) Characterization studies describe patient populations, baseline features, treatment patterns, temporal trends (example: Psoriasis patients) Outcome studies focus exposure definitions, time--risk, outcome specifications Treatment pathway studies detail era logic, gap collapsing rules, sequence analysis Note EGP file automatically generated launch study. template contains comments guidance help fill details. vignette teaches principles EGP construction shows examples different study types. ’ll adapt structure match research questions.

code: ### Newly-Diagnosed Psoriasis Cohort  #### Cohort Entry - First visit date with Psoriasis diagnosis code - Requirement: >= 2 Psoriasis diagnosis visits on different dates, 30-365 days apart - Requirement: 365 days continuous prior observation - Limit occurrence to the initial event per patient (first-ever diagnosis)  #### Inclusion Criteria - NO prior psoriasis-related treatments in 365 days prior to index  #### Cohort Exit - End of continuous observation, OR - Death ### Type 2 Diabetes Cohort  #### Cohort Entry - 2 codes of Type 2 Diabetes on different dates, at least 30 days apart - the second code is the index date - Limit occurrence to the initial event per patient (first-ever diagnosis)  #### Inclusion Criteria - NO occurrence of Type 1 Diabetes diagnosis code at any time prior to index date - NO occurrence of Gestational Diabetes diagnosis code at any time prior to index date  #### Cohort Exit - End of continuous observation, OR - Death

code: ### Prevalence Calculation: Any-Time Point Estimate  **Period of Interest:** Each calendar year 2015-2024  **Observation Requirements:** - Include: Anyone with >= 1 day enrollment in the year - Minimum continuous: None (any fragmented enrollment allowed)  **Lookback:** - Search 365 days prior to period for any Type 2 Diabetes diagnosis  **Numerator:** - Patients with Type 2 Diabetes diagnosis code prior to OR during period  **Denominator:** - All patients with any enrollment during period of interest  **Calculation:** Prevalence = (Numerator / Denominator) per 100,000 ### Baseline Characteristics  **Baseline Window:** 365 days prior to index date through 1 day prior  **Demographics Reported:** - Age at index date - Sex, Race, Ethnicity - Payer type - Calendar year of index  **Comorbidities:** - Report any diagnosis code during baseline window for:   - Autoimmune/Inflammatory conditions (Rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease, etc.)   - Cardiovascular disease   - Metabolic disease (Diabetes, Obesity)   - [Organized by clinical system]  **Treatments:** - Any dispensing during baseline window for:   - Topical agents (corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, retinoids)   - Systemic agents (methotrexate, acitretin, cyclosporine, apremilast)   - Biologic agents (TNF inhibitors, IL-17i, IL-23i, JAK inhibitors)   - Other (phototherapy, oral steroids)  ### Treatment Pathways During Follow-up  **Gap Collapsing Rules:** - Topical agents: Collapse gaps of <30 days - Systemic agents: Collapse gaps of <30-60 days depending on agent - Biologic agents: Collapse gaps of <60-120 days depending on specific drug  **Combination Logic:** - Different drug classes overlapping >= 60 days = counted as combination therapy  **Episode Minimum:** - Episodes of <14 days are excluded (too short to assess effectiveness)  **Output:** - Sunburst plot showing first 4 treatment steps in newly-diagnosed population - Table: Median days on treatment by therapy class and line number

previous_headings: Why Git and renv Matter for Picard Studies
title: Launching a Picard Study
text: Git tracks every change code documentation throughout project lifecycle. pipeline-driven studies, provides critical benefits: Code reproducibility: Git records exactly version code produced results. essential regulatory compliance peer review. Audit trail: Every commit includes made change, , . accountability crucial study documentation QC. Collaboration: Multiple team members can work different analysis tasks simultaneously without conflicts. Git helps merge changes cleanly. Pipeline provenance: pipeline generates results, can trace results back exact code commit produced . Disaster recovery: Git acts backup. something goes wrong, can revert previous working state. Feature branches: can test new analysis approaches isolated branches merging production. Picard’s Branching Model: Picard enforces strict branching workflow makes Git requirement, optional: Main branch: Protected branch used release-ready code. Production pipelines executed release branches created main. Develop branch: Integration branch team members merge tested features. testing QC happens code ready production. Feature/task branches: Individual developers work analysis tasks isolated branches, submit pull requests review merging develop. branching strategy ensures: - Production work never runs unstable code main - changes reviewed reaching production - Testing happens controlled environment deployment - Team members can work independently without interfering production results Without Git disciplined branching approach, safe way run production pipelines study multiple contributors. studies data security reproducibility paramount, Git optional—’s foundational. Note: Git automatically initialized create repository. specify gitRemote setup, need manually connect local repository remote push changes. See Setting Git Version Control section instructions.

title: Launching a Picard Study
text: R packages constantly updated. Different versions can produce different results, even identical data code. renv solves creating snapshot R environment: Reproducibility across time: renv.lock captures exact package versions used analysis. Six months six years later, can restore identical environment reproduce every result. Team consistency: collaborative studies, different team members might different package versions installed. renv ensures everyone uses versions, eliminating “works machine” problems. Dependency management: renv tracks just direct dependencies nested dependencies. package depends package B version 1.2, renv captures relationship. Production safety: promoting analysis code production, renv ensures dependencies compatible tested together. Regulatory compliance: studies subject validation requirements, renv provides documented evidence package versions captured reproducible. collaborative, regulated research environments, renv essential ensuring results truly reproducible team member point future. Note: Unlike Git, renv automatically initialized repository. must set renv . highly encouraged : - Ensures analysis produces consistent results run team members - Protects package updates silently break pipeline - Creates audit trail package versions used study See Setting renv Reproducibility section get started.

Place SQL files inputs/cohorts/sql/: SQL files must follow SqlRender conventions parameters prefixed @: Key SqlRender parameters: - @target_cohort_id — numeric ID cohort - @target_database_schema — schema results written - @cdm_database_schema — CDM database schema location - @vocabulary_database_schema — vocabulary schema location Always use DELETE INSERT make cohort idempotent (can re-run without duplication).
code: cohortManifest <- loadCohortManifest()  # Add a custom SQL cohort (the file must already exist in inputs/cohorts/sql/) cohortManifest$addSqlCohort(   filePath = here::here("inputs/cohorts/sql/my_custom_cohort.sql"),   label = "My Custom Cohort",   category = "Custom",   tags = list(source = "sql") ) -- Cohort: Patients with Type 2 Diabetes DELETE FROM @target_database_schema.cohort WHERE cohort_definition_id = @target_cohort_id;  INSERT INTO @target_database_schema.cohort   (cohort_definition_id, subject_id, cohort_start_date, cohort_end_date) SELECT   @target_cohort_id as cohort_definition_id,   person_id as subject_id,   condition_start_date as cohort_start_date,   DATEADD(day, 365, condition_start_date) as cohort_end_date FROM @cdm_database_schema.condition_occurrence WHERE condition_concept_id IN (201820, 443238)   AND condition_start_date >= '2015-01-01';

what: Build Pattern 5: Custom Dependent SQL Cohorts
title: Loading Inputs: Getting Started
text: Use pattern custom SQL cohort depends one previously defined cohorts (example inclusion/exclusion cohorts). registers cohort dependency-aware derived type (custom_derived) execution order, stale detection, dependency hashing handled automatically. Like built-derived cohort builders (subset, union, etc.), values supply rendered SQL immediately rendered file written inputs/cohorts/derived/<label>.sql — generated file, source file, ’s registered manifest. connection/schema placeholders (@target_cohort_id friends) left unrendered, generateCohorts() fill execution time. works: Preferred: manifest entry (data.frame/tibble id column, returned queryCohortsByLabel() similar query methods) — single row bakes one ID, multi-row table bakes comma-separated vector IDs, (@param) clauses. pattern baseCohortEntry/ cohortEntries built-derived builders. Backward compatible: raw integer cohort ID (integer vector). referenced cohort IDs must already exist manifest, become cohort’s depends_on parents staleness tracking. sqlParameters optional named mapping SqlRender parameter name value (thresholds, dates, strings, etc.) want baked SQL. treated cohort dependencies. rendered SQL registration time — runtime. dependentCohortIdList entries manifest entries label column, labels (purely QC) written generated comment header top derived SQL file — e.g. inc_cohort_id: id 1001, label Inclusion cohort — anyone reading generated file can see glance cohorts baked , without cross-referencing manifest. SQL file reference mapped placeholders: Required contract dependent custom SQL: Must DELETE @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table using @target_cohort_id. Must INSERT @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table columns (cohort_definition_id, subject_id, cohort_start_date, cohort_end_date). ensures custom dependent SQL cohorts behave consistently derived cohorts manifest review pipeline execution. dependency internals (dependency graph ordering, dependency_rule storage, stale/hash behavior), see Manifest Management.
code: cohortManifest <- loadCohortManifest()  # Preferred: entries from manifest query results inclusionEntry <- cohortManifest$queryCohortsByLabel("Inclusion cohort") exclusionEntry <- cohortManifest$queryCohortsByLabel("Exclusion cohort")  cohortManifest$addDependentCustomCohort(   filePath = here::here("inputs/cohorts/sql/my_custom_dependent.sql"),   label = "Eligible_With_Exclusions",   category = "Derived Cohorts",   dependentCohortIdList = list(     inc_cohort_id = inclusionEntry,     exc_cohort_id = exclusionEntry   ),   # Optional: any other values (not cohort IDs) to render into the SQL too   sqlParameters = list(     min_days = 30L   ),   tags = list(owner = "epi_team", source = "custom_sql") ) DELETE FROM @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table WHERE cohort_definition_id = @target_cohort_id;  INSERT INTO @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table   (cohort_definition_id, subject_id, cohort_start_date, cohort_end_date) SELECT   @target_cohort_id,   i.subject_id,   i.cohort_start_date,   i.cohort_end_date FROM @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table i LEFT JOIN @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table e   ON i.subject_id = e.subject_id   AND e.cohort_definition_id = @exc_cohort_id WHERE i.cohort_definition_id = @inc_cohort_id   AND e.subject_id IS NULL;

text: common workflow custom cohorts template sql file build multiple variations custom cohort template. user needs make two folders: inputs/cohorts/R/src - folder holding R functions put templates together inputs/cohorts/R/src/sql - folder holding sql templates render R function. example. study needed create derived custom cohort called censored complement. First provide custom sql need place inputs/cohorts/R/src/sql folder. Notice template using cohorts already created building custom derivation analyze. want several inclusion/exclusion pairs manifest. addDependentCustomCohort() renders dependentCohortIdList/sqlParameters SQL writes result inputs/cohorts/derived/<label>.sql , template file inputs/cohorts/R/src/sql can reused -, unmodified, every pair — ’s need hand-copy pre-render first. apply sql template R function build custom derived cohort manifest: addDependentCustomCohort() reads sqlTemplatePath, renders @inc_cohort_id/ @exc_cohort_id literal cohort IDs, writes result generated file inputs/cohorts/derived/ — template safely reused across calls, since call produces uniquely named output (named label), never overwriting template another cohort’s file. templating strategy can also applied $addSqlCohort, render bake parameters file — keep template inputs/cohorts/R/src/sql pre-render (example SqlRender::render()) registering, since addSqlCohort() registers whatever file ’s given -.
code: /* Make a censored complement. This means find all persons who do not have the exclusion ever or track them until the day before the exculsion criteria occurs.  For example I want exclude anyone with CKD prior to T2D. But include T2D persons who had CKD after index date up till the day before CKD index.  */  DELETE FROM @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table WHERE cohort_definition_id = @target_cohort_id;  INSERT INTO @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table (cohort_definition_id, subject_id, cohort_start_date, cohort_end_date)  WITH T1 AS ( /* Find the persons where the exclusion is after the inclusion start date Adjust the end date to the day before the combination of three occurs */ SELECT     a.subject_id,     a.inc_cohort_start_date AS cohort_start_date,     a.exc_cohort_start_date - 1 AS cohort_end_date FROM (   SELECT     inc.subject_id,     inc.cohort_start_date AS inc_cohort_start_date,     inc.cohort_end_date AS inc_cohort_end_date,     exc.cohort_start_date AS exc_cohort_start_date,     exc.cohort_end_date AS exc_cohort_end_date,     ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inc.subject_id ORDER BY inc.cohort_start_date) AS rn   FROM @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table inc   INNER JOIN @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table exc     ON inc.subject_id = exc.subject_id AND exc.cohort_definition_id = @inc_cohort_id   WHERE inc.cohort_definition_id = @exc_cohort_id     AND exc.cohort_start_date >= inc.cohort_start_date ) a  UNION ALL  /* Find the persons where the exclusion never occurs to those with the inclusion */ SELECT   pop.subject_id,   pop.cohort_start_date,   pop.cohort_end_date FROM @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table pop LEFT JOIN (   SELECT     subject_id   FROM @target_database_schema.@target_cohort_table   WHERE cohort_definition_id IN (@exc_cohort_id)   GROUP BY subject_id   HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cohort_definition_id) >= 1 ) excluded   ON pop.subject_id = excluded.subject_id WHERE pop.cohort_definition_id = @inc_cohort_id   AND excluded.subject_id IS NULL ) SELECT   @target_cohort_id AS cohort_definition_id,   subject_id,   cohort_start_date,   cohort_end_date FROM T1; buildCensoredComplement <- function(   cohortManifest,   inclusionEntry,   exclusionEntry,   inputsDir = here::here("inputs/cohorts/R") ) {    sqlTemplatePath <- fs::path(inputsDir, "src/sql/censored_complement.sql")    cohortLabel <- glue::glue("{inclusionEntry$label[1]} - {exclusionEntry$label[1]} exclusion")    check_if_there <- is.null(cohortManifest$queryCohortsByLabel(cohortLabel))   if (!check_if_there) {     cli::cli_alert_warning("Censored Complement {.val {cohortLabel}} already exists. Skipped!")   } else {     cli::cli_alert_info("Create Censored Complement for {.val {cohortLabel}}")     cohortManifest$addDependentCustomCohort(       filePath = sqlTemplatePath,       label = cohortLabel,       category = "Target Sub Pop",       dependentCohortIdList = list(         inc_cohort_id = inclusionEntry,         exc_cohort_id = exclusionEntry       )     )   }    invisible(cohortLabel) }

title: Manifest Management
text: Rebuilding derived pipeline new parameters → "derived". base cohort registrations ATLAS imports preserved; just re-run $build*() calls. Corrupt restructured database → "manifest". Source files kept; call initCohortManifest() re-register via $add*() $importAtlasCohorts(). Complete restart → "full". Requires executionSettings drop OMOP tables. text: manifest provides two methods viewing cohort metadata: Interactive Viewing (Recommended Exploration) Programmatic Tabulation (pipelines/analysis)
code: # Open an interactive RStudio viewer with streamlined metadata # Shows: id, label, category, tags, file_path manifest$viewManifest()  # Filter to specific status manifest$viewManifest(filter = "active") manifest$viewManifest(filter = "stale") manifest$viewManifest(filter = "deleted")  # Control tag format in the viewer: # - nested (default): tags as structured tibble with tag_name/tag_value # - json: tags as raw JSON string # - wide: tags expanded into individual columns manifest$viewManifest(tags_format = "nested") manifest$viewManifest(tags_format = "wide")  # Excel-like view # Full tabular view with all columns (id, label, category, tags, file_path, hash, source_type, cohort_type, status, depends_on, created_at, deleted_at) tbl <- manifest$tabulateManifest()  # Filter by status stale_cohorts <- manifest$tabulateManifest(filter = "stale") deleted_cohorts <- manifest$tabulateManifest(filter = "deleted") all_cohorts <- manifest$tabulateManifest(filter = "all")  # Control tag format # Option 1: nested (default) - tags as nested tibble with tag_name/tag_value pairs tbl_nested <- manifest$tabulateManifest(tags_format = "nested") # Access nested tags: tbl_nested$tags[[1]] returns a tibble of tag pairs  # Option 2: json (backward compatible) - tags as raw JSON string tbl_json <- manifest$tabulateManifest(tags_format = "json") # Useful for APIs or custom tag parsing  # Option 3: wide - tags expanded into individual columns # Creates one column per unique tag key across the manifest tbl_wide <- manifest$tabulateManifest(tags_format = "wide") # Columns like: id, label, category, file_path, hash, status, approval_status, domain, etc.

title: The Ulysses Standard Repository Structure
text: Picard built Ulysses framework, follows philosophy real-world evidence (RWE) studies organized versioned software projects. Just databases require schema organize data, RWE studies benefit standard directory structure organize code, inputs, analyses, outputs. standardization enables: Reproducibility: Anyone can understand project structure glance Collaboration: Multiple contributors follow conventions Automation: Consistent organization enables reliable workflows tooling Version control: Clear separation concerns makes git history meaningful Picard uses Ulysses repository structure, adding specialized directories configuration cohort-based studies, Evidence Generation Plans, results dissemination. vignette describes standard Ulysses repository structure created initialize project using launchUlyssesRepo().

title: The Ulysses Standard Repository Structure
text: Ulysses repository organizes folders match flow real-world evidence study: Workflow sequence: 1. Initialize metadata (config.yml defines databases credentials) 2. Load create inputs (cohorts concept sets) 3. Execute analysis tasks (code analysis/tasks runs using inputs) 4. Raw results written exec/results organized database version 5. Post-processing: runPostProcessing() merges raw results across databases dissemination/export/merge/, reference files QC reports 6. Dissemination: numbered scripts dissemination/pretty/R/ format merged results via sourceDisseminationScripts(); Study Hub (quarto website) renders narrative results together
code: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 1. META & CONFIG                                                │ │    (config.yml, README.md, NEWS.md, main.R, test_main.R)       │ │         ↓                                                        │ │ 2. INPUTS                                                       │ │    inputs/cohorts/ + inputs/conceptSets/                      │ │    (Define phenotypes, cohorts, covariates)                    │ │         ↓                                                        │ │ 3. ANALYSIS                                                     │ │    analysis/tasks/ + analysis/src/                              │ │    (Execute analyses, generate statistics)                      │ │         ↓                                                        │ │ 4. EXECUTION OUTPUT                                             │ │    exec/results/[database]/[version]/[task]/                  │ │    (Raw results by task, database, version)                     │ │         ↓                                                        │ │ 5. POST-PROCESSING & DISSEMINATION                              │ │    dissemination/export/merge/ + dissemination/pretty/ +       │ │    dissemination/quarto/                                        │ │    (Merge results, format for release, build Study Hub website) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

text: Central configuration file specifying parameters needed establish database connections. Uses YAML format two section types: default: Universal study settings (project name, version) block headers: Database-specific configurations (dbms, credentials, schemas) source block header task file, pipeline runs using block’s configuration, enabling multi-database studies. Important: Connection details vary database system. codebase distinguishes : Snowflake: Uses connectionString format (JDBC connection string) PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, Redshift: Use server port fields Protecting Credentials !expr: !expr tag (config package) allows evaluate R code within config file. critical security: enables pulling credentials environment variables rather storing plain text config.yml. can use R function wrapped !expr retrieve credentials, including: Environment variables: !expr Sys.getenv('VAR_NAME') Keyring package: !expr keyring::key_get(service = 'picard', username = 'atlasUser') Custom functions: !expr my_secure_fetch_credential('db_password') Best practice: Always use !expr secure credential storage system. Never store passwords connection strings plain text config.yml commit git. Common credentials: dbms: Database type (snowflake, sql server, postgresql, mysql, oracle, redshift) user: Database username (environment variable via !expr Sys.getenv()) password: Database password (environment variable) databaseName: Internal reference name (snake_case database + snapshot date) databaseLabel: Pretty name output formatting cdmDatabaseSchema: Schema containing OMOP CDM tables (format: schema database.schema) vocabDatabaseSchema: Schema containing vocabulary tables (usually cdmDatabaseSchema) workDatabaseSchema: Schema user write access (cohort tables intermediary work) tempEmulationSchema: Optional schema temp tables (snowflake, oracle) cohortTable: Name cohort table create (default: {repoName}_{databaseName}) Example config.yml Snowflake PostgreSQL: Setting environment variables: .Renviron file (project home directory): Load running pipeline: readRenviron("~/.Renviron")

Columns: - atlasId: ATLAS concept set ID (integer, e.g., 456, 789) - label: Display name (character, e.g., "Antidiabetic medications") - category: Broad grouping (character, e.g., "Medications" "Diagnoses") - subCategory: Optional sub-grouping (character, e.g., "Endocrine Drugs") - domain: OMOP clinical domain (required, character): - drug_exposure - Medication/drug concept sets - condition_occurrence - Diagnosis concept sets - measurement - Lab/test result concept sets - procedure - Medical procedure concept sets - observation - Observation concept sets - device_exposure - Device/equipment concept sets - visit_occurrence - Visit type concept sets - init - yet classified (placeholder) - sourceCode: Rarely used; TRUE concept set represents source codes instead standard concepts (character: TRUE FALSE) - file_name: Relative path JSON file (character, e.g., "json/hypertension.json") Example: loaded, metadata fields converted tags concept set querying (e.g., $getConceptSetsByTag(), $getConceptSetsByLabel()). conceptSetManifest.sqlite: SQLite database created/managed ConceptSetManifest class. Contains concept_set_manifest table: Workflow: Create update conceptSetsLoad.csv metadata (use createBlankConceptSetsLoadFile()) Import ATLAS concept set JSON definitions json/ folder (use importAtlasConceptSets()) Call loadConceptSetManifest() scan directories enrich conceptSetsLoad.csv metadata First load creates conceptSetManifest.sqlite database; subsequent loads verify file hashes Use ConceptSetManifest methods query: $getConceptSetById(456), $getConceptSetsByTag("domain: drug_exposure") Extract source codes dependencies using $extractSourceCodes() (requires ExecutionSettings) See also: Loading Inputs detailed guidance creating, importing, managing concept set manifests.
code: inputs/conceptSets/ ├── json/ │   ├── exposure_antidiabetic.json        # Drug exposure concept set │   ├── outcome_mi.json                   # Condition outcome concept set │   └── covariate_hypertension.json       # Covariate measurement concept set ├── conceptSetsLoad.csv                   # Metadata index for concept set enrichment └── conceptSetManifest.sqlite             # Provenance & metadata tracking database atlasId,label,category,subCategory,domain,sourceCode,file_name 456,Antidiabetic Medications,Medications,Endocrine,drug_exposure,FALSE,json/exposure_antidiabetic.json 789,Acute MI,Diagnoses,Cardiovascular,condition_occurrence,FALSE,json/outcome_mi.json 1001,Hypertension,Diagnoses,Cardiovascular,condition_occurrence,FALSE,json/covariate_hypertension.json

title: Using Agent Skills for Cohort and Concept Set Development
text: Step 1: Open agent invoke skill agent chat, ask something like: Step 2: Answer agent’s questions agent ask: - cohort ? (disease, exposure, outcome, medication, procedure) - inclusion criteria? (e.g., least one T2D diagnosis) - exclusion criteria? (e.g., type 1 diabetes, pregnancy) - date constraints? (e.g., index date, lookback window) - cohort registered? (label, category, tags) Step 3: Review refine agent generates Capr code. can: - Ask agent modify specific logic - Copy code paste import_capr_cohort.R - Run script register cohort manifest Step 4: Register cohort Capr definition, agent helps call:
code: I want to build a T2D cohort using Capr. Can you help me? Use the capr-cohort-generation skill to help me build a cohort. manifest$addCaprCohort(   caprCohort = your_cohort_def,   label = "T2D on Metformin",   category = "target",   tags = list(source = "capr", status = "approved") )

title: Using Agent Skills for Cohort and Concept Set Development
text: Step 1: Open agent invoke skill Step 2: Confirm base cohorts exist agent ask name parent cohort(s). verify exist manifest: cohort found, agent stops — must add manifest first. Step 3: Choose builder type agent asks kind derived cohort want: buildSubsetCohortTemporal() — Temporal window (e.g., specific date range) buildUnionCohort() — Union (e.g., combine two definitions) buildComplementCohort() — Exclude subjects (e.g., T2D without CKD) buildCompositeCohort() — Intersection (e.g., subjects 2+ cohorts) buildDemographicCohort() — Filter age/gender/race buildStratifiedCohorts() — Split subgroups buildOPriorT() buildTPriorO() — Outcome/exposure temporal relationships buildCensorCohort() — Censoring logic Step 4: Specify builder parameters Depending builder type, agent asks : - Temporal subset: Start window, end window (e.g., “90 days prior index” “end follow-”) - Union: cohorts combine - Complement: cohort base, exclude - Demographic: Age range, gender, race/ethnicity filter - Stratification: split (e.g., age groups: <65, 65+) Step 5: Review confirm agent generates builder code build_dependent_cohorts.R shows summary top code added:
code: I want to build a derived cohort. Can you help me? Use the picard-dependent-cohorts skill to help me build a dependent cohort. Parent cohort: T2D ✓ Found: T2D (id=3, active) # ============================================================================ # Builder: T2D on Metformin at Baseline # ============================================================================ # Type: Temporal Subset # Base: T2D (id=3) # Filter: Metformin (id=12) # Window: 1 year prior to index, same day index # ============================================================================  manifest$buildSubsetCohortTemporal(   label = "T2D_on_Metformin_at_baseline",   baseCohortId = 3,   filterCohortId = 12,   category = "derived",   startWindow = createSubsetStartWindow(startDays = -365),   endWindow = createSubsetEndWindow(endDays = 0),   tags = list(type = "temporal_subset", parent = "T2D"),   stopIfExists = FALSE )

title: CLAUDE.md
text: picard R package (OHDSI/Boehringer Ingelheim) building running reproducible, pipeline-based real-world evidence (RWE) studies. two distinct things: Scaffolds study repositories (“Ulysses” repos) — standardized folder structure, config files, manifests, starter scripts individual research study. Provides runtime library generated study repos depend — manifest management, execution settings, task tracking/validation, post-processing, dissemination helpers. repo package — study repo. Study repos UlyssesStudy$initUlyssesRepo() generates elsewhere disk (see tests/testthat/helper-init.R pattern used tests). Note: files inst/agent/ (AGENTS.md, numbered reference docs, skills/) templates copied generated study repos, documentation package — ’re written instructions AI agent helping analyst inside study repo ({{placeholder}} variables, restricted code-execution policy, OMOP CDM guidance, etc.). Don’t confuse constraints (e.g. “never execute pipeline”) constraints working repo. initUlyssesRepo()/initAgentMode() install AGENTS.md + .agent/ study repo, alongside Capr package’s capr-cohort-generation skill bundle Capr installed.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: standard R package using devtools/testthat/roxygen2. CI workflow R CMD check/tests (.github/workflows/pkgdown.yml docs) — validate locally. Roxygen uses markdown (Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) DESCRIPTION) — always run devtools::document() touching roxygen comments, never hand-edit man/*.Rd NAMESPACE.
code: devtools::load_all()          # load package for interactive dev devtools::document()          # regenerate NAMESPACE/man/*.Rd from roxygen comments — run after any @export or param change devtools::test()              # run full testthat suite devtools::test_active_file()  # run just the currently open test file testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-CohortManifest-query.R")  # run one test file directly devtools::check()             # full R CMD check pkgdown::build_site()         # rebuild docs/ site (vignettes + reference)

what: R6 classes are the core abstraction
title: CLAUDE.md
text: Almost stateful behavior lives R6 classes (R/*.R), plain exported functions thin, user-facing constructors/wrappers around (e.g. makeStudyMeta() wraps StudyMeta$new(), makeBlock() wraps DbConfigBlock$new()). adding feature, check whether belongs method existing class adding free function. UlyssesStudy (R/Ulysses.R) — orchestrates initUlyssesRepo(): creates folder structure, README/NEWS/config.yml, Quarto study hub scaffold, main.R, agent-skill files, initializes git. entry point “create new study.” ExecutionSettings (R/ExecutionSettings.R) — wraps DB connection (ConnectionDetails) plus schema/table names (cdmDatabaseSchema, workDatabaseSchema, tempEmulationSchema, cohortTable, databaseName). Must provide exactly one connectionDetails connection, never . Built either directly (createExecutionSettings()) config.yml block (createExecutionSettingsFromConfig()). DbConfigBlock — one database’s worth config (feeds config.yml blocks ExecutionSettings). CohortManifest / ConceptSetManifest (R/CohortManifest.R, R/ConceptSetManifest.R — two largest files, 4500 2200 lines) — track cohort/concept-set definitions rows SQLite database (inputs/cohorts/cohortManifest.sqlite, inputs/conceptSets/conceptSetManifest.sqlite). entry id, label, tags, file path, content hash (change detection), type, timestamp, soft-delete status. CohortDef/ConceptSetDef corresponding single-item value objects. R/manifest_helpers.R provides top-level wrapper functions (initCohortManifest(), loadCohortManifest(), etc.) plus query/visualization utilities classes. R/migrateCohortManifest.R / R/migrateConceptSetManifest.R handle schema migrations sqlite files across package versions. R/cohort_builders.R — dependency-graph logic derived cohorts (subset/union/complement) depend cohorts manifest. Task execution (R/execute.R, R/taskTracking.R, R/validation.R) — study’s analysis/tasks/*.R files follow mandatory 5-section format (. Meta, B. Dependencies, C. Connection Settings, D. Task Settings, E. Script) enforced validateStudyTask(). shouldRerunTask() decides whether re-run task based file hash, dependency hashes, manifest hash, version changes, recording history exec/logs/task_run_history.csv. Tasks numbered (01_, 02_…) executed order execStudyPipeline()/testStudyPipeline(). Post-processing/dissemination (R/postProcess.R, R/disseminate.R, R/studyHub.R) — importAndBind()/orchestratePipelineExport() merge per-database, per-version, per-task result CSVs exec/results/ dissemination/export/merge/; migration scripts reshape dissemination/export/pretty/ studyHubOutput/. studyHub.R builds Quarto-based “Study Hub” website README/NEWS + exported result files. R/secrets.R — DB/Atlas credentials live user-level secrets.yml (default ~/.picard/secrets.yml), never study repo. Supports !expr YAML tags (e.g. Sys.getenv(), keyring::key_get()) resolved via resolveSecretValue(). R/git.R — git workflow helpers (saveWork(), agentSaveWork(), createAgentBranch(), createPullRequest(), validateCodeState()) built gert, used humans agent-driven workflows enforce branch discipline (never commit/push directly main). R/renv.R — renv setup/snapshot/restore helpers reproducible study environments. R/WebApi.R — WebApiConnection R6 class + helpers importing cohorts/concept sets OHDSI ATLAS instance. R/make.R — bulk file-generation helpers (makeTaskFile(), makeSrcFile(), makeBlock(), makeDisseminationScript(), etc.) used initUlyssesRepo() afterward analysts add new tasks/cohorts.

what: Manifest storage pattern (important when touching CohortManifest/ConceptSetManifest)
title: CLAUDE.md
text: manifests follow shape: R6 class wraps SQLite table, connections opened/closed per-operation (DBI::dbConnect … .exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(conn))), rows carry content hash used detect drift manifest -disk cohort/concept-set files, soft-deletes use status/deleted_at column rather row removal. Tags stored single serialized string ("key: value | key2: value2") parsed back via expandManifestTags()/parseTagsString(). add column behavior one manifest, check whether parallel manifest needs change — ’re maintained lockstep, including migration files.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Task-level/user-facing functions: camelCase (generateCohorts, validateStudyTask). Internal snake_case helpers exist (e.g. check_git_status, build_dependency_graph) — snake_case signals “internal implementation detail,” camelCase signals “public API.” Package functions namespaced explicitly (dplyr::filter(), checkmate::assert_string()) rather attached via library(). Input validation via checkmate::assert_*() top exported functions; user-facing errors/progress via cli::cli_alert_*, cli::cli_abort(), cli::cli_bullets() rather base warning()/message(). R6 private fields prefixed leading dot (private$.dbPath, private[[".repoName"]]).

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Tests live tests/testthat/, run via testthat::test_check("picard") (see tests/testthat.R). Helpers: - helper-init.R — make_test_repo_for_file_creation() builds full temp Ulysses repo (via real initUlyssesRepo() flow) tests need realistic repo disk. - helper-Manifest.R — cm_test_make_manifest_paths() / cm_test_new_manifest() build isolated temp inputs/cohorts tree + fresh CohortManifest manifest tests, avoiding cross-test state. - test_files/ — fixture cohort/concept-set JSON SQL files used manifest tests. Test files split class/concern (test-CohortManifest-builders.R, -lifecycle.R, -management.R, -query.R, -review.R), one file per source file — follow split (behavior, file) adding cohort-manifest tests rather creating new test-CohortManifest-<newfeature>.R per source file.
